items.title: backlog add --title/--intent shortcuts: add items without raw JSON
items.intent: Running backlog add --title "..." --intent "..." must create a new backlog item without requiring the caller to construct a JSON string — so developers can add items ergonomically from the command line without quoting hell.
items.description: backlog add currently requires --json with a full JSON object string, which is verbose and error-prone for quick ad-hoc adds. A flag-based shorthand (--title, --intent, --priority, --track, --desc, --type) constructs the JSON internally and reuses existing validation.
steps: In cmd_backlog_add() (lib/cmd-backlog-write.sh:28), detect when first arg is NOT --json and NOT --help (i.e., it is a flag like --title)
Parse flags: --title, --intent, --priority (default: should), --track (default: feature), --desc, --type (default: feat) using a while loop
After parsing, require at minimum --title and --intent; error and exit 1 if either is missing
Construct JSON from parsed flags using jq -n and pass as raw_json to the existing add logic (starting at line 55 validate JSON block)
Update cmd-help.sh backlog add entry to show both usage forms

acceptanceCriteria.text: help backlog documents flag-based add syntax

   else
       # Flag-based shorthand: --title "..." --intent "..." [--priority P] [--track T] [--desc "..."] [--type feat|bug]
       local _title="" _intent="" _priority="should" _track="feature" _desc="" _type="feat"
       while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
           case "$1" in
               --title)    _title="${2:-}";    shift 2 ;;
               --intent)   _intent="${2:-}";   shift 2 ;;
               --priority) _priority="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
               --track)    _track="${2:-}";    shift 2 ;;
               --desc)     _desc="${2:-}";     shift 2 ;;

               *) log_error "Unknown flag: $1"; _backlog_add_usage; return 1 ;;
           esac
       done
       [[ -z "$_title" ]]  && { log_error "--title is required"; _backlog_add_usage; return 1; }
       [[ -z "$_intent" ]] && { log_error "--intent is required"; _backlog_add_usage; return 1; }
       raw_json=$(jq -n \
           --arg title "$_title" --arg intent "$_intent" \
           --arg priority "$_priority" --arg track "$_track" \
           --arg desc "$_desc" --arg type "$_type" \
           '{"title":$title,"intent":$intent,"priority":$priority,"track":$track,"description":$desc,"type":$type}')

items.title: backlog check --json: machine-readable readiness output
items.intent: Running backlog check --all --json must output a JSON array of per-item readiness objects and exit 0 — so scripts and CI can inspect readiness state programmatically without parsing human-formatted table output.
items.description: backlog check outputs a human-readable pass/fail table. A --json flag emits structured output: for --all, an array of {id, ready, failures} objects; for a single item, a single {id, ready, failures} object. Exit 0 always in --json mode (caller reads the ready field).
